Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Global Assurance Holdings Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Assurance Holdings' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; David Lee, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Chen, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Michael Rodriguez, Chief Claims Officer; and Anna Wong, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Global Assurance Holdings' performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by our conservative asset allocation strategy across fixed income, equities, and alternatives; meaningful dividend increases to $0.82 per share; expanded investment income yields reaching 4.28%; a fortified capital position with $8.7 billion in statutory surplus; the positive effects of pricing adjustments on premium volume growth; elevated policy retention rates across major lines averaging 87.2%; favorable updates to actuarial assumptions adding $285 million to earnings; and robust new business production of $3.2 billion in premiums and 1.25 million policies. Our commitment to innovation and customer service continues to drive our success.

Sarah Thompson, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Mark. Good morning, everyone. As Mark mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $500 million, or $2.41 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included underwriting profitability, higher investment returns, premium growth from pricing discipline, retention gains, favorable reserve developments, strong capital returns, and operational efficiencies. Our combined ratio was 92.4%. Investment income for the quarter was $1.8 billion. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with $8.7 billion in statutory surplus. Our expense ratio also improved to 28.2%.

Let me expand on a few of these highlights, starting with our capital position and statutory surplus levels. As of the end of Q3 2024, our consolidated statutory surplus reached $8.7 billion, reflecting a 10% increase year-over-year from $7.9 billion and a 2% sequential rise from Q2. This robust growth stems from consistent underwriting execution, solid investment income in a higher-rate backdrop, and strategic reserve adjustments in our property and casualty operations. It places us firmly above our $8.0 billion internal target and in the upper echelon of peers like Chubb and Travelers, per S&P Global data.

Our risk-based capital ratio stands at an impressive 325% consolidated, surpassing the 200% regulatory company action level and our 300% internal benchmark—up 15 points from year-end 2023. P&C is at 340%, life and annuity at 315%, and health at 290%, balancing expansion needs like Medicare Advantage with surplus builds from retained earnings. Retained earnings added $650 million in the quarter, supported by our leading 92.4% combined ratio despite $450 million in cat losses from wildfires and hurricanes. Investment income contributed $420 million, with yields up to 4.6%, and unrealized AFS gains turned positive by $250 million as Treasury yields stabilized near 4.1%.

U.S. operations, 65% of premiums, drove much of this with $5.6 billion surplus up 12% YoY, aided by E&S lines and rehedged wildfire risks via Swiss Re. Europe grew 8% to €1.8 billion equivalent on motor renewals, while Asia-Pacific surged 15% to $1.1 billion from life sales in Japan and Singapore, capturing 18% annuity market share per LIMRA. We've advanced our ORSA with climate stress tests against 1-in-250-year events using RMS and KCC models, optimizing $2.5 billion in cat reinsurance at 85% ceding commissions. FHLB funding pilots provide $500 million low-cost liquidity for life liabilities.

This strength enables $1.2 billion in share repurchases—$800 million YTD at $105 average—and an 8% dividend hike to $1.05 quarterly, yielding 2.9%. We're eyeing $800 million in M&A for cyber and parametric lines, plus $300 million from pension transfers. We project $9.2-9.5 billion surplus by year-end, RBC over 320%.

Turning to our dividend payments, our Board declared $0.82 per share quarterly, payable November 15 to October 25 record holders—a 6.3% YoY rise from $0.77, lifting TTM to $3.24 and annualized yield to 2.9% at $112.50 share price, competitive with Travelers at 2.1% and Chubb at 1.2%. Over 10 years, CAGR is 7.2% versus S&P Insurance Index 5.8%, backed by $145 billion portfolio and Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.41 up 12% on 92.4% combined ratio below industry 96.5%. Payout is 45% of TTM EPS, in 40-50% target, with $1.2 billion free cash flow.

Underwriting cats moderated to $450 million versus $620 million last year; ex-cat loss ratio improved to 61.2% on 8.2% premium growth and telematics/climate models. Investments yielded 4.6% on corporates and municipals. U.S. 93.1% ratio, Europe 91% via Lloyd's, Asia health up 14% despite typhoons. RBC 420% U.S., Solvency II 185% Europe. DRIP uptake up 25% at 2% discount; ESG-linked increases targeting 20% carbon reduction; $2.5 billion buyback with $800 million YTD. Guide 5-7% growth at 14.5% ROE, with $5 billion specialty pipeline and Bermuda reinsurer buy.

Next, our investment income yield hit 4.28% annualized, up 35 bps QoQ from 3.93% and 62 bps YoY from 3.66%, on net income over average assets excluding reinsurance funds withheld. This ALM execution supports P&C and life margins.

Fixed income (78%) yielded 4.62% up from 4.12% YoY: corporates (42%) at 5.01% like JPMorgan; munis (15%) 3.85% tax-efficient AA GO bonds; RMBS/ABS (12%) 5.45% Ally auto. Duration 5.8 years matches liabilities; 92% IG A- average, OAS 112 bps over Barclays 85 bps.

Equities/alts (22%): equities 6.2% on S&P ETFs, dividend aristocrats 3.1%; alts 7.8% REITs 5.9% Prologis, BREIT infra 8.2%. Low volatility, duration beta 0.92.

Regions: U.S./Canada 82% at 4.55%; Europe 12% 3.95% gilts/BTPs; APAC/EM 6% 7.2% Singapore/AUD. Initiatives: ALM ladder +50 bps on $18 billion maturities via Aladdin; ESG 35% Article 8; equity puts +12 bps. Outperforms NAIC 3.9%, peers; Sharpe 1.42. Every 10 bps adds $14 million income; guide 4.3-4.5% FY with $22 billion liquidity.

Finally, changes in actuarial assumptions delivered $285 million favorable pre-tax impact, 12% of EPS beat. Discount rates up: P&C 3.2% to 4.1% SOFR+50 bps ($120 million release), life 3.8% to 4.5% ($60 million), Europe milder $25 million. $2.5 billion swaps hedge duration.

Mortality/longevity: 2017 to 2020 CSO blended, -4% early/-2.5% late (A/E 92%), PRT/anuity -6 months ($65 million total). UK/Canada conservative $10 million.

Trends unfavorable offset: auto PD 8.2% to 5.6% trend ($95 million strengthen), WC medical 5.2%, cats +15% RMS v18. APAC typhoons $30 million, U.S. BI favor $25 million. GLMx ML on Snowflake 92% accuracy; telematics lapses.

Expect $100-150 million quarterly favorability; cat bonds $500 million H2. Reserves 95% confidence for 10-12% ROE.

David Lee, over to you for underwriting.

David Lee: Thank you, Sarah. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our property and casualty lines. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophes and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including advanced analytics and dynamic pricing strategies.

Specifically, on the impact of pricing changes, we applied 7.8% average adjustments, up from 6.2% in Q2, addressing social inflation and 3.1% CPI services. GWP grew 4.2% YoY to $2.85 billion despite 1.8% policy dip—rate outpacing volume.

Personal lines (62%): auto +5.6% to $1.12 billion on -2.4% PIFs, 9.1% rate via telematics (28% book, tiered 4-15%); homeowners +6.8% flat volume, 8.5% rate, RMS climate models +20% high ZIPs, 92% retention.

Commercial (38%): +2.9% to $1.08 billion, -0.5% PIFs, 5.2% rate; E&S +12% volume/11.5% rate, blockchain quotes -35% time.

Regions: U.S. 85% +5.1% on -1.2% volume, CA/FL filings; Europe flat -2.1%, bundled +14%; APAC +9.2% +4% EV telematics -22% claims.

Ties to 92.6% ratio, 13.4% ROE. Genie AI 92% trends; 90.5% retention; cheaper reinsurance. Guide Q4 4-6% growth, 7-8% rate.

Policy retention rates averaged 87.2% overall, +140 bps YoY, 11th straight gain over AM Best 83%/81%. Personal auto 89.5% +210 bps, Telematics 2.0 2.8M users -8% frequency, 12% discounts, lapses 10.5%. Homeowners/renters 86.8% +90 bps, Horizon Shield satellite alerts -15% non-renews coastal 84.2%, bundling +22%. Commercial P&C 82.4% +320 bps >78% avg, parametric 48hr payouts, 92% pricing acceptance, WC flexible. Life/annuity 94.2%, 4.8% crediting.

Regions: NE/MW 88.9%, SE 85.1%, West 83.7% WILDFIRE rebound, int'l 86.5%. Pillars: myHorizon 92% self-service -18% costs; CLV 47 cohorts +4.2%; partnerships Uber/Sunrun. Q4 +50-100 bps, 7-8% premiums, 14% ROE.

New business production hit $3.2 billion premiums +18% YoY (+20% FX), 1.25M policies +22%, best since Q4 2021 > AM Best 12%. P&C $2.1B +25%: auto 850K policies +28%, DriveSafe UBI 45% -15% LR; cyber $180M +45%, parametric DORA 24hr quotes. Life/health $1.1B +8%, 400K policies; UL $700M +12% Wells Fargo; ACA/group +20% ADP.

Regions: U.S. 75% $2.4B +21% 4.2% share; Europe $500M +12% UK fleet; APAC $300M +35% India 150K UPI; LatAm +5%. 16% 6Q CAGR >11% index, 92% persistency. Accelerate factory -22% NBAC $450/policy, genAI 30% faster; RMS v18 +15% pricing; quota 20% Munich. Cat bond $1.2B. Q3 14-17%, FY $13.5-14B 17%, parametric wildfire/indexed annuities. NBM 28% +200bps.

Robert Chen: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income, equities, and alternatives.

Our general account assets are $258 billion, up 4% YoY on premium growth offset by LDI outflows, supporting $220 billion reserves. Duration 6.8 vs 7.2 liabilities, 180 bps new spread, earned 5.8% YTD +120 bps Bloomberg Agg. Navigated 4.1% 10yr, 110 bps IG spreads, 2.5-3% inflation.

Fixed income 72% $186B down from 75%, yield 4.6% +70 bps: Treas/MBS 28% $52B 4.8% Fannie/Freddie liquidity 120% surrenders; IG corp 42% $78B A- 5.2yr financials/utilities +$450M NAV; ABS/CMBS 15% $28B 5.5% Ally/Ford <0.2% default; HY/EM 4% $7.4B BB energy/Indonesia. U.S. 65%, Europe 20% covered Deutsche/Nordea, APAC 10% AUD. Aladdin/ML stress +200bps ICR 4.5x.

Equities 16% $41B +2pts, outpace 3.2% crediting: public 85% $35B 60/40 S&P/EAFE 8.2% Q3 tech/health, div 2.1% Sharpe 0.85; PE 15% $6B KKR/Apollo 12-15% IRR. U.S. 70%, Europe Stoxx, Asia Nikkei. VIX options cap -15% RBC NAIC.

Alts 12% $31B +1pt peers trend, 7-9% IRR beta 0.25: real assets 40% $12.4B Prologis/data 6.8%; PE 35% $10.9B Blackstone secondaries 18% DPI; infra/hedge 25% $7.7B Orsted/Bridgewater. NA 55%, Europe 30% UK debt, Asia 15% India roads. Blockchain portal -20% admin +$2B commitments, 45% ESG SFDR >Solvency II.

Outlook: 70/15/15 de-risk if rates <3.75%, alts to 14% GP stakes, +50bps ROE vs Athene/Corebridge.

Michael Rodriguez: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including AI-driven processing and parametric triggers, resulting in reduced processing times to under 48 hours for many events and improved resolution rates above industry averages.

Lisa Patel: As COO, we've optimized operations across regions, leveraging digital tools for efficiency.

Anna Wong: We are making significant investments in technology to enhance our operations and improve the customer experience. Our new Aladdin-integrated ALM platform and Genie AI stack, along with blockchain portals and telematics apps like Horizon Shield and DriveSafe, are driving efficiencies, cutting costs by up to 20%, and enabling faster quoting and personalized service.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Doe with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Doe: Good morning. Can you provide more color on your new business growth momentum?

Mark Thompson: Good morning, John. Absolutely. As David detailed, our $3.2 billion in new premiums and 1.25 million policies reflect strong execution in P&C and life, powered by digital factories, UBI penetration at 45%, and regional expansions like India micro-insurance. This builds embedded value with 92% persistency and 28% NBM, positioning us for 17% full-year growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jane Smith with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Jane Smith: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of higher interest rates on your business?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, Jane. Higher rates have been a significant tailwind, boosting investment yields to 4.28% and enabling $180 million favorable discount rate changes. Our ALM duration matching and swaps hedge volatility, supporting surplus growth and annuity crediting competitiveness while stabilizing combined ratios.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson: What is the expected impact of new IFRS 17 requirements on your underwriting strategy?

David Lee: Good morning, Mike. IFRS 17 enhances transparency on CSM releases, and our European book at 92% ratio is well-positioned. We've adjusted pricing and reinsurance—15% cheaper cat cover—to maintain margins, with no material shift in risk appetite; focus remains on rate adequacy and retention over 86%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Can you elaborate on the expected benefits of the new technology platform?

Anna Wong: Good morning, Emily. Our platforms like Aladdin, Genie AI on Google Cloud, and blockchain portals process petabytes of data for 92% accurate trends, 35% faster quotes, 92% self-service renewals, and 18-22% cost reductions. This accelerates new business, boosts retention via personalization, and optimizes underwriting for climate risks, targeting $250 million savings.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Wilson with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Tom Wilson: Thanks. On retention, how sustainable is 87%+ amid rate hikes?

David Lee: Great question, Tom. Sustainability comes from value delivery—telematics discounts, Shield alerts, parametric speed—driving 90.5% overall vs. JD Power 87%. CLV segmentation and partnerships lift it further; expect continued gains to support 7-8% earned growth.

Operator: [Potentially more questions]

Mark Thompson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Global Assurance Holdings. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
